passages.original: In lectulo (in- quit) meo, hoc est, cum adhuc in desideriis carnali- bus requiescerem, et cum adhuc infidelitatis et igno- rantiae tenebris posita essem, quaesivi quem diligit anima mea. Multi enim philosophorum Deum igno- rantes, studio tamen summo illum requirebant, per creaturam Creatorem cognoscere volentes, sicut Plato, qui in Timaeo multa de anima disputavit, et sicut Aristoteles, Socrates et caeteri, qui omne vitae suae tempus in studiis causa exquirendae veritatis expendebant. Quaesivi illum, et non inveni; non enim per mundanam sapientiam Deus cognosci potuit.
passages.english: "On my little bed," she says, that is, while I was still resting in carnal desires, and while I was still set in the darkness of unbelief and ignorance, "I sought him whom my soul loves." For many of the philosophers, though ignorant of God, nevertheless sought him with the greatest zeal, wishing to know the Creator through the creation: such as Plato, who in the Timaeus discussed many things about the soul, and such as Aristotle, Socrates and the rest, who spent the whole time of their lives in studies for the sake of searching out the truth. "I sought him, and did not find [him]"; for God could not be known through worldly wisdom.
